item.title: Hero dad who stopped Oregon school shooter shares his story
item.description: 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco shared his story with Oregon Public Broadcasting a week after the school shooting that killed three children and a teacher.

item.title: DOJ sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Sullivan loses
item.description: The Trump administration is suing to prevent the Alaska Senate election from being certified if GOP Sen. Daniel Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola because of the other Dan Sullivan who is on the ballot.

item.title: Police officer who shot and killed 1-year-old resigns
item.description: The Mississippi attorney general's office had determined that the use of force was justified in the deadly shooting that stemmed from an alleged shoplifting incident.

item.title: What to expect from Brewers-Rays World Series
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are set to host the Tampa Bay Rays Friday night in Game 1 of the World Series. Levi Weaver, staff writer for the Athletic, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: France to deploy 70,000 police officers Saturday as it prepares for more mass protests
item.description: The police presence is being boosted across France as it braces for another weekend of anti-government protests. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry has more.

item.title: 60 Minutes investigates "third-country deportations"
item.description: As the Trump administration seeks to carry out the largest deportation in American history, it is removing more and more people to countries they are not from and often have no ties to. It's called "third-country deportation." A 60 Minutes investigation reveals how some of these third countries are forcing deportees back to the nations they fled, places where U.S. immigration judges have ruled they could not be sent because they'd likely face persecution or torture.

item.title: Colorado, Utah contend with heavy flooding
item.description: Multiple states are dealing with severe weather, including flooding and gusty winds. Rob Marciano has the details.

item.title: Officer who fatally shot 1-year-old in Walmart parking lot resigns
item.description: Hunter Foster, the police officer who fatally shot a 1-year-old boy who was sitting in his mother's lap in a Walmart parking lot in Mississippi has resigned despite being cleared of criminal wrongdoing. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: U.S. ambassador to U.N. says Iran war could last another year
item.description: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told the Financial Times in a new interview that the Iran war could last another year. CBS News' Olivia Gazis has more.

item.title: Meet the hero dad who took down the Oregon elementary school shooter
item.description: Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old father of two, happened to find himself outside his daughters' elementary school in Bend, Oregon, when he spotted an armed figure. Carter Evans has the story.

item.title: House hunter discovers body in vacant home
item.description: In an exclusive interview, a homebuyer shares vivid details of finding a dead man during a house tour.

item.title: Extended interview: Son of freed American Stephen Hubbard, Fr. Joseph Coleman, on father's release
item.description: The son of Stephen Hubbard, Fr. Joseph Coleman, and the family's lawyer, Martin De Luca, speak with CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi about Hubbard's release from Russia after more than four years in jail.

item.title: Trump continues to back Ramaswamy's attack ad, campaigns in Florida with midterms 11 days away
item.description: President Trump on Friday doubled down on his support for Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad against Amy Acton featuring Acton's estranged mother. Mr. Trump also headed to the Sunshine State to campaign for Florida gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds. CBS News' Cristian Benavides and Ed O'Keefe have more.

item.title: Judge allows Jane Doe anonymity in Cornell sexual assault lawsuit
item.description: Jane Doe can remain anonymous in her sexual assault lawsuit involving former members of Cornell University's Chi Phi fraternity, a judge ruled.

item.title: How Thomas Jefferson politicked his way into the Louisiana Purchase
item.description: The Louisiana Purchase was the biggest territorial expansion in American history. A new book, "Jefferson's Landmark Deal," examines the unique role President Thomas Jefferson played in that monumental acquisition. Author and public scholar Lara Brown, who is also Major Garrett's wife, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Angie Nixon: Democrats are underinvesting in Florida because "they think that the state is racist"
item.description: Florida Democratic Senate candidate Angie Nixon says she thinks donors aligned with her party have underinvested in the Sunshine State because they believe it is racist. Political strategists Mike Hahn and John McCarthy join with analysis.

item.title: Unpacking early voting trends in North Carolina and Florida
item.description: More than 15 million Americans have already voted early in the 2026 midterm elections. VoteHub head of data science Zachary Donnini joins "The Takeout" with a look at the numbers.

item.title: Democrat hoping to flip Nebraska House seat pushing for action on affordability
item.description: One of the congressional seats Democrats are eyeing as a potential flip is Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District. Candidate Denise Powell joins "The Takeout" to discuss her priorities if elected to the House.

item.title: Kushner denies upcoming book claim that he received billions in slush funds
item.description: U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner is denying allegations in an upcoming book by journalist Matthew Cole that he received more than $2 billion in slush funds from Middle East leaders. CBS News homeland security correspondent Nicole Sganga has the details.

item.title: Top Ukrainian diplomat says SpaceX satellite access is still restricted
item.description: Ukrainian officials say their access to the SpaceX satellite service remains restricted, despite President Trump's claim that Elon Musk has fully restored access. Denys Sienik, Chargé d'Affaires at the Embassy of Ukraine in the U.S., joins to discuss that and the temporary ceasefire first lady Melania Trump helped secure in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city.

item.title: Sen. Thom Tillis, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Gina Hinojosa set to appear on "Face the Nation"
item.description: Sunday's "Face the Nation" is set to feature Republican Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Texas Democratic gubernatorial nominee Gina Hinojosa. CBS News chief foreign affairs correspondent and "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan joins to preview the show.

item.title: Justice Department sues to block Alaska Senate race results if Republican loses
item.description: At President Trump's direction, the Justice Department sued Friday to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race if Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, citing the presence of another candidate on the ballot bearing the same name. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe has more.

item.title: Deadly shooting in Paris suburb investigated as terrorism, officials say
item.description: A gunman opened fire from his car in the Paris suburb of Trappes on Friday, in what authorities described as a racially motivated act of terrorism.

item.title: Trump lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods in boon to Sen. Susan Collins
item.description: President Trump on Friday slashed tariffs on a handful of Canadian products that are used widely by Maine's agricultural industry, a move cheered by GOP Sen. Susan Collins, who is facing a tough reelection battle.

item.title: How Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield are shaping the war in Ukraine
item.description: Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield satellite networks play different roles in Ukraine's fight against Russia. Here's how the two systems work, how they're used on the battlefield and why Ukraine's reliance on them could be a vulnerability.

item.title: UFO files detail strange, silent triangular craft: "Absolute acoustic silence"
item.description: Federal agents encountered a large aircraft that zoomed across the sky from a standstill while making no noise or giving off any exhaust, according to new files.

item.title: 10/23: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Justice Department sues to block Alaska Senate race results if Republican loses; 11 days until midterm contests.

item.title: Trump's U.N. ambassador says Iran war could drag on for another year
item.description: The U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says the war with Iran could last another year, but he hopes Tehran will "come to the table" sooner.

item.title: Meghan "deeply distressed" as dad faces child abuse material probe
item.description: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is facing a probe in the Philippines over alleged possession of child sexual abuse materials.

item.title: Why a California DA is holding parents responsible for kids' electric motorcycle accidents
item.description: A California district attorney is holding parents responsible for serious electric motorcycle accidents involving their children. Natalie Morales has more.
